metadata.title: APR File Format Specification — rule catalog
metadata.remarks: Derived from docs/APR_SPECIFICATION.md by scripts/build-oscal.py. The specification is normative; where this catalog disagrees with it, the catalog has the defect.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The format version **MUST NOT** track releases. Two releases that do not change the wire format declare the same format version, and that is correct.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-SEC-001 says the format version must not track releases. That binds how this project versions itself; no document and no implementation can violate it.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: `aprVersion` **MUST** be exactly `"1.0-beta.6"`. A record declaring any other value **MUST** be rejected with `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`, including `1.0-beta`, `1.0-beta.3`, and any later beta.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-SEC-002 is covered. APR-SEC-003 restates unknown-member preservation, which its own rules cover, and APR-SEC-004 explains what BETA means to an implementer. Neither adds an obligation a document or an implementation could fail.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Unknown-member preservation ([Unknown members](#extensions)) is unaffected and remains **REQUIRED**. It is what keeps additive change safe within a version.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-SEC-002 is covered. APR-SEC-003 restates unknown-member preservation, which its own rules cover, and APR-SEC-004 explains what BETA means to an implementer. Neither adds an obligation a document or an implementation could fail.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **What BETA means here:** breaking changes are intentional until the first public release. Implementers **SHOULD** record the corpus tag they pass, not just the format version.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-SEC-002 is covered. APR-SEC-003 restates unknown-member preservation, which its own rules cover, and APR-SEC-004 explains what BETA means to an implementer. Neither adds an obligation a document or an implementation could fail.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A core-only implementation given a stream **MUST** report `APR_STREAM_REQUIRES_ITERATION` and **MUST NOT** select a record by position.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-CONF-001 is core-only behaviour: a single-form API handed a stream must report APR_STREAM_REQUIRES_ITERATION and must not select a record by position. The harness asks whether a document was accepted, not which API was called. Reaching it needs the profile-scoped run tracked separately.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A core-only implementation **MUST NOT** reject a stream containing attestations, and **MUST** preserve attestation records on round-trip.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-CONF-005, that a core-only implementation never reports a document as verified and should say attestations are present but unchecked, is about what it displays. The harness scores acceptance, not wording.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A core-only implementation **MUST NOT** reject a document that uses expressions and **MUST** preserve the expression strings when writing it back. A host rendering the document presents those prompts as ordinary editable fields: a computed field simply becomes a field the user can type into — degraded, but never broken, and never lost.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Preservation by a core-only reader has no dedicated vector.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An implementation **MUST NOT** claim a profile without passing the corpus revision it names.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Within a run the harness holds a claimed profile to every case in it, so a declaration that is not answered for fails. Whether the declaration published outside the harness is honest is not machine-checkable.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It **MUST NOT** report a document as verified, and **SHOULD** indicate that attestations are present but unchecked. Saying nothing is better than saying verified; saying "present, unchecked" is better than both.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-CONF-005, that a core-only implementation never reports a document as verified and should say attestations are present but unchecked, is about what it displays. The harness scores acceptance, not wording.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A `prompt.response` **MUST** be a JSON string, and a response given as a JSON number or boolean **MUST** be rejected at parse time.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 malformed fixture carries a non-string response.

controls.title: APR-MODEL-002 — 4.8 Any string is a valid response

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A response **MAY** contain any string. The format has no opinion about whether that string is "correct".

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every member of `prompt.hints` is advisory. A hint **MUST NOT** cause a response to be rejected, altered, truncated, or blocked from being saved. This applies to `validationPattern` — a non-matching response is a warning at most — and to every member of the `expr*` family.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Advisory behavior is gated in client tests; no beta.6 corpus vector asserts it.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An implementation **MAY** surface a hint mismatch as an advisory warning. It **MUST NOT** prevent the user from saving.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Advisory behavior is gated in client tests; no beta.6 corpus vector asserts it.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It **MUST NOT** be coerced to `"42"` or `"true"`. Rejecting and coercing are different failures: one refuses the document, the other accepts it having invented data.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 malformed fixture carries a non-string response.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information is discarded deliberately when moving from presentation to model. Source trivia **MUST NOT** carry APR meaning, and a writer is under no obligation to reproduce it. Everything else — including members APR does not define — **MUST** survive a round trip.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A document **MUST** be encoded as UTF-8 (RFC 3629). A byte-order mark **SHOULD NOT** be written; a reader **SHOULD** tolerate a leading one.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-REP-002, 003 and 004 concern the byte layer: UTF-8 encoding, a byte-order mark, ill-formed sequences, U+0000 and unpaired surrogates. The suite carries documents as text in a JSON file, so it cannot express a malformed byte sequence. Reaching them needs the suite to carry encoded bytes rather than strings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A reader **MUST** reject ill-formed UTF-8 rather than substituting replacement characters silently.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-REP-002, 003 and 004 concern the byte layer: UTF-8 encoding, a byte-order mark, ill-formed sequences, U+0000 and unpaired surrogates. The suite carries documents as text in a JSON file, so it cannot express a malformed byte sequence. Reaching them needs the suite to carry encoded bytes rather than strings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every string **MUST NOT** contain U+0000, and **MUST NOT** contain an unpaired surrogate in the range U+D800 to U+DFFF. Control characters U+0001 through U+001F **MUST NOT** appear, except tab (U+0009), line feed (U+000A), and carriage return (U+000D), which are permitted so that a multiline response can hold the line breaks a person typed.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-REP-002, 003 and 004 concern the byte layer: UTF-8 encoding, a byte-order mark, ill-formed sequences, U+0000 and unpaired surrogates. The suite carries documents as text in a JSON file, so it cannot express a malformed byte sequence. Reaching them needs the suite to carry encoded bytes rather than strings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Once comments and trailing commas are removed, the text **MUST** decode as JSON (RFC 8259) to the semantic model. Comments are source trivia and cannot carry APR meaning.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **One constraint the grammar cannot express.** RFC 8259 §4 says object member names SHOULD be unique. APR raises this: a parser **MUST** reject a duplicate member name rather than applying a last-key-wins rule.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **MUST** be a well-formed YAML 1.2.2 document, per that specification's character, structural, flow, block, and document-stream productions (chapters 5 to 9).

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Only anchors have a vector. Tags, merge keys, non-finite numbers, binary, implicit dates and constructors are unexercised.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **MUST** resolve every scalar to a value of the JSON data model (RFC 8259): null, boolean, number, string, array, or object, and nothing else.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Only anchors have a vector. Tags, merge keys, non-finite numbers, binary, implicit dates and constructors are unexercised.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **MUST** resolve every mapping key to a string.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Only anchors have a vector. Tags, merge keys, non-finite numbers, binary, implicit dates and constructors are unexercised.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **MUST NOT** use the constructs excluded below.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Only anchors have a vector. Tags, merge keys, non-finite numbers, binary, implicit dates and constructors are unexercised.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A plain scalar denoting a non-finite float — `.inf`, `-.inf`, `.nan`, in any capitalization — **MUST** be rejected. JSON has no representation for it, so there is no value for it to resolve to.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-REP-008, 011, 012 and 017 are covered. APR-REP-013 requires a safe loader that never constructs a host-language object from document content. Proving that needs inspection of the reader, and a document that would exploit an unsafe loader is already refused by the excluded-constructs rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An implementation therefore uses a YAML library for **syntax** — characters, structure, flow and block style, document streams — and **MUST NOT** use that library's default scalar resolution.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-REP-008, 011, 012 and 017 are covered. APR-REP-013 requires a safe loader that never constructs a host-language object from document content. Proving that needs inspection of the reader, and a document that would exploit an unsafe loader is already refused by the excluded-constructs rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Implementations **MUST** use a safe loader: one that constructs only the JSON Schema value types and never instantiates a host-language object from document content.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-REP-008, 011, 012 and 017 are covered. APR-REP-013 requires a safe loader that never constructs a host-language object from document content. Proving that needs inspection of the reader, and a document that would exploit an unsafe loader is already refused by the excluded-constructs rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: `null` is not an APR value. A writer **MUST NOT** emit it. A reader tolerates it in a response position only, coercing it to the empty string; anywhere else it is a parse failure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every other member is **structural**: it describes the form rather than carrying what a person typed. A structural member uses the **JSON type that fits it**, natively: a flag is a JSON boolean, a count is a JSON integer, a numeric bound is a JSON number, and a name, identifier, or piece of text is a JSON string. A writer **MUST** emit each structural member in the type its member table declares, and a reader **MUST** report a structural member of another type as `WRONG_TYPE` ([Errors](#structural-validation)). `"canAddRows": "true"` is not a boolean and `"maxRows": "25"` is not a count.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Where JSON has no type for a value, the member is a string in a stated form: timestamps are RFC 3339 strings, and a bound on a temporal field is a string in that field's canonical write form ([Canonical value forms](#canonical-values)). A structural member is never a string *because* it is structural; it is a string only when a string is the fitting type.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Responses remain strings even where a scalar would otherwise resolve as a number or boolean under the JSON Schema, because [Responses are strings](#responses) governs the semantic model regardless of how a scalar resolved. Anywhere else, an author who means the *string* `true` or `25` — as a suggested value, say — **MUST** quote it, exactly as a JSON author must; the table above is the only thing that decides.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-REP-008, 011, 012 and 017 are covered. APR-REP-013 requires a safe loader that never constructs a host-language object from document content. Proving that needs inspection of the reader, and a document that would exploit an unsafe loader is already refused by the excluded-constructs rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: `sections` — array — **Yes** — **MUST** contain at least one section.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A form **MUST NOT** carry a `signatures` member. A reader encountering one **MUST** report `RETIRED_EMBEDDED_SIGNATURES` ([Retired members](#retired-members)).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: `title` **MUST** contain a non-whitespace character.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-037, that workflow state is not form data, forbids this document from defining a member rather than forbidding anything a document may contain. A receiver recording a date in an owned extension member is conforming, so no vector separates compliance from violation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When `documentType` is `filledForm`, `templateId` is **REQUIRED**: a completed form that cannot name the form it completes is not traceable.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-037, that workflow state is not form data, forbids this document from defining a member rather than forbidding anything a document may contain. A receiver recording a date in an owned extension member is conforming, so no vector separates compliance from violation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A section **MUST** carry content: at least one prompt or at least one child section. There is no exception — tables included.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Section ids and prompt ids occupy **separate namespaces**: a section and a prompt **MAY** share an id. Within each namespace, ids **MUST** be unique across the whole document, not merely among siblings — a filled form is consumed by field id, and a duplicate makes the data ambiguous.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ids are compared by exact code-point equality; no normalization, case folding, or trimming is applied. Ids **SHOULD** be stable across template versions and **MUST NOT** change when prompts are reordered. Reordering a form is a presentation change; changing an id silently breaks every downstream consumer and every attestation covering it.

controls.title: APR-MODEL-012 — 5.6.2 A table licenses no layout

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A renderer **MAY** present a table as a grid, as stacked cards, as a flat sequence of prompts, or as speech. **All are conformant**, and none is a fallback.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 corpus fixture carries a table section.

controls.title: APR-MODEL-013 — 5.6.2 A table licenses no layout

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A table **MUST NOT** be treated as licence for width, alignment, colour, or font data. Those member names are retired ([Retired members](#retired-members)) and are dropped on read.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 corpus fixture carries a table section.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Instances **SHOULD** agree in prompt count and in the label at each position. When they disagree the document is still **valid**; a validator reports `TABLE_RAGGED` or `TABLE_LABEL_MISMATCH` and a renderer presents what is there.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 corpus fixture carries a table, ragged or otherwise.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Sections nest recursively. Every implementation **MUST** support at least **16 levels** of section nesting. Implementations **MAY** support more.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-015 is covered by a sixteen-level vector. APR-MODEL-016 and 017 cannot be: one forbids an author from relying on a ceiling above the floor, and the other asks authors to stay well below it. Both bind the person writing a form, and no document is wrong for ignoring either.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Any particular ceiling above that floor is an implementation detail and **MUST NOT** be relied upon by a document author.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-015 is covered by a sixteen-level vector. APR-MODEL-016 and 017 cannot be: one forbids an author from relying on a ceiling above the floor, and the other asks authors to stay well below it. Both bind the person writing a form, and no document is wrong for ignoring either.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authors **SHOULD** stay far below the floor. Forms nested more than four or five levels deep are difficult to navigate with any input method.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-015 is covered by a sixteen-level vector. APR-MODEL-016 and 017 cannot be: one forbids an author from relying on a ceiling above the floor, and the other asks authors to stay well below it. Both bind the person writing a form, and no document is wrong for ignoring either.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **This registry is open.** An unrecognized value **MUST** degrade to a plain text field. It **MUST NOT** cause an error — that is what lets the registry grow without breaking every existing reader.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 fixture exercises an unregistered expectedDataType degrading to text.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A response outside them is **still valid**, exactly as for `suggestedValues`. A slider that stops at 100 does not make `120` a wrong answer, and a validator **MUST NOT** reject one. Bounds shape the affordance offered to someone who wants it; they never shrink what a person is allowed to say.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 fixture exercises an unregistered expectedDataType degrading to text.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A reader **MUST** ignore members it does not recognise, at every level, and **MUST NOT** reject a document for carrying them.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A reader **MUST** also **preserve** them: an unrecognised member present on read **MUST** still be present, unchanged, on write.

controls.title: APR-MODEL-022 — 5.9.1 Retired members are the exception

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: `signatures` is reported rather than silently dropped: a reader **MUST** report `RETIRED_EMBEDDED_SIGNATURES`, because a document carrying it was making a cryptographic claim that beta.6 cannot honour, and losing that silently would be worse than refusing it.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A reader **MUST** accept every listed read form. A writer **SHOULD** emit the canonical form. Neither rule ever makes a document invalid.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **Why newline and not comma for `multichoice`.** A suggested value may itself contain a comma — `Bloomfield, CT` is an ordinary option in a municipal form. Comma separation silently turns one selection into two, which is data loss. A newline cannot appear inside a single-line option, so the encoding is lossless. Readers **MUST** still accept the legacy comma form.

controls.title: APR-MODEL-025 — 5.11 Roles — who each part is for

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A section or a prompt **MAY** carry `role`: a short string naming who is meant to fill it in. A prompt's role overrides the role of the section containing it, so a single field can be handed back to the patient without splitting the section in two. The vocabulary is **open**: a reader that does not recognise a role **MUST** present the field normally rather than erroring.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-025 and 026 are covered. APR-MODEL-027 and 028 are reader behaviour: that a role never decides who may type, and that a reader should make roles legible including to assistive technology. A document declaring roles is valid whether a reader honours them or ignores them. APR-MODEL-050 is reader behaviour: falling back to the identifier when a role has no name, and showing an undeclared role rather than erroring. A document is valid either way.

controls.title: APR-MODEL-026 — 5.11 Roles — who each part is for

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each entry **MUST** carry `id`; `name` and `description` are OPTIONAL.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-025 and 026 are covered. APR-MODEL-027 and 028 are reader behaviour: that a role never decides who may type, and that a reader should make roles legible including to assistive technology. A document declaring roles is valid whether a reader honours them or ignores them. APR-MODEL-050 is reader behaviour: falling back to the identifier when a role has no name, and showing an undeclared role rather than erroring. A document is valid either way.

controls.title: APR-MODEL-027 — 5.11 Roles — who each part is for

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **A role says who a field is for. It never says who may type into it.** The format has no identity at fill time — nothing in a document knows who is at the keyboard — so a reader **MUST NOT** refuse input to a field because of its role.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-025 and 026 are covered. APR-MODEL-027 and 028 are reader behaviour: that a role never decides who may type, and that a reader should make roles legible including to assistive technology. A document declaring roles is valid whether a reader honours them or ignores them. APR-MODEL-050 is reader behaviour: falling back to the identifier when a role has no name, and showing an undeclared role rather than erroring. A document is valid either way.

controls.title: APR-MODEL-028 — 5.11 Roles — who each part is for

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: What a reader **SHOULD** do is make the answer obvious without being asked. Where a document declares roles, a reader **SHOULD** let the person say which role they are filling and then show plainly which fields are theirs. Fields belonging to others stay visible and stay editable; they are marked, not locked. A reader **SHOULD** also make a role legible to assistive technology, since a visual treatment alone communicates nothing to a screen reader.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-025 and 026 are covered. APR-MODEL-027 and 028 are reader behaviour: that a role never decides who may type, and that a reader should make roles legible including to assistive technology. A document declaring roles is valid whether a reader honours them or ignores them. APR-MODEL-050 is reader behaviour: falling back to the identifier when a role has no name, and showing an undeclared role rather than erroring. A document is valid either way.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **An extension member is named by its owner.** An extension member name **MUST** begin with a reverse-DNS prefix owned by the producer, followed by a dot: `com.example.priority`, `gov.ct.dmv.routing`. A reader identifies an extension member by the dot in its name. A validator **MAY** report an unrecognised undotted member as `UNPREFIXED_MEMBER`; it **MUST NOT** reject the document, and **MUST** still preserve the member ([Warnings](#warnings)).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **There is no `signature` type and no `file` type.** A signature is not a response: evidence that a person stood behind a form is an attestation record travelling beside it in the stream ([Attestations](#attestations)), never a drawn image or a typed name in a field. An attachment is not a response either: a form carries what a person typed, and the format defines no representation for bytes that were not typed. A reader encountering either name treats it as any other unregistered value and degrades it to text.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 fixture exercises an unregistered expectedDataType degrading to text.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **Unprefixed names belong to the specification.** Every member this document defines is unprefixed, and every member a later version of APR adds will be. A producer **MUST NOT** add a member whose name carries no prefix.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A `submissionUrls` entry is one of exactly two kinds, told apart by its scheme. This document defines no other transport.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Transport behaviour is outside the corpus. No test yet asserts that an unsupported scheme is reported or refused.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **`https`.** The entry is a URL to which the complete document is delivered by a single HTTP `PUT`, with the document as the body and the `vnd.apr` media type of its representation as `Content-Type` ([Document type](#media-types)). The URL is used verbatim, query string included: this is the contract of an S3 pre-signed PUT URL, which carries its own authorisation and expiry in the query, and any receiver that accepts a plain `PUT` of a body satisfies it identically. A client **MUST** send only the document — no credentials, cookies, or headers derived from it — **MUST** treat any status other than 2xx as failure, **MUST NOT** follow a redirect, and **MUST NOT** retry without a fresh user action.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Transport behaviour is outside the corpus. No test yet asserts that an unsupported scheme is reported or refused.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **`mailto`.** The entry is an RFC 6068 address, with any header fields it carries such as `subject` passed through. Submitting means composing a message to that address with the **stream** as a single attachment, never inlined in the body; a lone form is a one-record stream. A client **SHOULD** hand the composition to the user's mail client, and **MAY** instead send natively if it has that ability; either way the message leaves only on an explicit user action.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Transport behaviour is outside the corpus. No test yet asserts that an unsupported scheme is reported or refused.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each transport is **OPTIONAL** and claimed separately ([Declaring conformance](#declaring-conformance)). A client **MUST NOT** act on an entry whose scheme it does not recognise or does not implement, and a validator **SHOULD** report an entry of a scheme this document does not define as `SUBMISSION_URL_UNSUPPORTED` ([Warnings](#warnings)). An `http` entry is unsupported.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Transport behaviour is outside the corpus. No test yet asserts that an unsupported scheme is reported or refused.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **Template identity.** `templateId` **MUST** be a URI (RFC 3986). It identifies; it need not resolve. The **RECOMMENDED** form is a tag URI (RFC 4151), `tag:skpt.cl,2026:dog-license`, which is unique by construction — it is minted from a domain or email address the author held on a date — and needs no server. Any URI the author controls the uniqueness of is acceptable, an email address as a `mailto` URI included. A reader **MUST NOT** fetch a `templateId`.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-037, that workflow state is not form data, forbids this document from defining a member rather than forbidding anything a document may contain. A receiver recording a date in an owned extension member is conforming, so no vector separates compliance from violation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **Workflow state is not form data.** When a form was received, by whom, and what happened to it next are facts the *receiver* tracks against the form, not members of it. This document defines no member for them, and a workflow that needs to record them writes its own form and names what that form was about ([Related records](#regarding)), never adding them to a form somebody else wrote.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-MODEL-037, that workflow state is not form data, forbids this document from defining a member rather than forbidding anything a document may contain. A receiver recording a date in an owned extension member is conforming, so no vector separates compliance from violation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A table introduces **no new primitive**. Rows are ordinary sections; cells are ordinary prompts. A section becomes a table by carrying `kind: "table"`, and **only** by carrying it: a table is never inferred from `maxRows`, `canAddRows`, or the presence of child sections, and those members on a section that is not a table are preserved and ignored.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **A hint a reader cannot use is not an error.** A hint that is unrecognised, unsupported, or malformed — an unparseable `validationPattern`, a bound of the wrong type, an expression that will not compile — **MUST** be preserved and **MAY** be reported as a warning; it **MUST NOT** make the document invalid. Hints are applied in the order the member table lists them, and where two hints on one prompt conflict, the earlier one stands and the later one is skipped and **MAY** be reported.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No beta.6 fixture exercises an unregistered expectedDataType degrading to text.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An author names things. A writer **MUST** preserve every valid id it read, and **MUST NOT** invent or replace an id unless the caller explicitly asks it to repair the document; by default a blank id or a duplicate is simply the error [Errors](#structural-validation) says it is.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No vector yet asserts the generation algorithm; a digest vector for the three worked ids belongs beside the digest fixtures.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A blank or whitespace-only id receives a generated one. Where two members share an id, **both** are renamed, since neither has a better claim to the name than the other.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: No vector yet asserts the generation algorithm; a digest vector for the three worked ids belongs beside the digest fixtures.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Generated ids are short, typeable, and carry no order: two adjacent prompts get unrelated names, and nothing about a name says where it sits. A writer **MUST NOT** generate ids that encode position — `q1`, `q2`, `row_3` — because a person reading them will take the sequence to mean something, and inserting one row would then appear to renumber the rest. A renamed id is a changed id, with everything the stability rule above warns of: a `fields` attestation naming the old id resolves to nothing afterwards, which is the honest outcome, since the thing it named is no longer there under that name.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Reader behaviour: that a form without an attestation is ordinary, that parsing and extraction never wait on verification, and that refusing to act is a host policy rather than a format rule. A document is valid either way, so no vector distinguishes a conforming reader from one that gates.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **A proof MAY carry a claimed signing time.** In `cms/ecdsa-p256-sha256` that is the CMS signing-time signed attribute (RFC 5652), which sits inside the signature and therefore cannot be altered without breaking it. What nothing vouches for is the clock: the value is the signer's assertion that they signed then, and no more. A reader that shows it **MUST** show it as claimed rather than proven, and **MUST NOT** derive from it that one record precedes another.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-ATTEST-014, that a claimed signing time is shown as claimed rather than proven, is about how a reader labels a value. The corpus carries a CMS proof with a signing time, and nothing distinguishes an implementation that presents it honestly from one that presents it as trusted time.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **What that protection is, exactly.** `subject.digest` names the complete form, so an edit anywhere produces a changed form, and against *that* form the attestation is `unresolved` rather than invalid ([Changed forms](#changed-forms), [Verification vocabulary](#verification)). It stays `valid` against the form it was made over, which is why a workflow retains the original record rather than replacing it. A verifier **MUST NOT** report `invalid` merely because the form it holds is a later one.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: APR-ATTEST-005 is covered. APR-ATTEST-006, 015 and 016 are verifier behaviour: that an unrelated edit is never reported as invalid, that a later form leaves an attestation unresolved rather than invalid, and that a verifier may report per-path which attested values still match. All three are about what a verifier says, and the harness scores documents rather than verification reports.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A verifier **MAY** additionally compare a `fields` manifest's entries against a changed form and report which attested paths still match. That is a diagnostic and **MUST NOT** be reported as a verification result: the attestation remains an assertion about its original subject and is never transferred to another.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A renderer **MAY** paginate, group, or lazily load, but **MUST NOT** reorder. A wizard that shows one section at a time still visits them in array order.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: A renderer obligation, not a property of a document: array order is in the file either way, and only a rendering can reorder it. Reaching it portably would need the harness to observe presentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Exports to PDF, HTML, or print **MAY** introduce layout — page size, margins, footers. That layout belongs to the renderer's options and **MUST NOT** be written back into the APR document. The document stays presentation-free no matter how many ways it has been rendered.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: About what an exporter must not write back into the document. The suite has no export step, and adding one would mean specifying an export format, which the specification deliberately does not.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **No executable content.** APR contains no scripts, macros, formulas with host access, or external references. Opening an APR document from an untrusted sender executes nothing. This is the format's most important security property and **MUST NOT** be weakened. Expressions are pure, bounded, and non-Turing-complete; they are not an exception.

parts.name: assessment-gap
parts.prose: Three properties of an implementation rather than of a document. No executable content is a property of the format itself — there is nothing to execute — so nothing can violate it. No network access on open and resource bounds need the harness to observe a reader's behaviour, not its answer. Resource bounds are partly gated in-repo by ParserFuzzTests.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: **No network access on open.** Reading a document **MUST NOT** fetch anything. `submissionUrls` is data — no entry **MUST** be contacted without an explicit user action, and neither **MUST** a certificate endpoint.
